explanation: In females, hormonal cycles coordinate the ovarian cycle, which consists of two main phases: the follicular phase and the luteal phase. During the follicular phase, Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) promotes the development of an ovarian follicle, which subsequently secretes estrogens. During the luteal phase, Luteinizing Hormone (LH) promotes the development of the corpus luteum, which then secretes progesterone.

questions.q: What hormone stimulates follicle development during the follicular phase, and what hormone does the developing follicle secrete?
opts: LH stimulates follicle development; the follicle secretes progesterone.
FSH stimulates follicle development; the follicle secretes estrogens.
GnRH stimulates follicle development; the follicle secretes testosterone.
HCG stimulates follicle development; the follicle secretes LH.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide states that in the Follicular Phase: 'FSH promotes the development of a follicle' and 'Follicle then secretes estrogens.'

questions.q: What is the role of Luteinizing Hormone (LH) in the luteal phase of the ovarian cycle?
opts: It promotes the development of the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone.
It stimulates the follicle to release estrogens.
It acts on the hypothalamus to shut down GnRH.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide states that in the Luteal Phase: 'LH promotes development of the corpus luteum' and 'Corpus luteum then secretes progesterone.'
